solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Load from tip heading off

indicators.note: heading off says the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a tip is a bonus, an extra payment for service

explanation.surface: Someone carries a load away from the rubbish tip, setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a rubbish dump but is a gratuity; 'heading off' strips the B from BONUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or responsibility is a load one has to bear.

clue.text: Mixed tofu up with a European stew

indicators.note: mixed says the letters that follow are stirred into a new order, like stew ingredients

explanation.surface: A cook throws tofu into a European stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' shuffles TOFU, UP, A and E together into the French dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The French dish of boiled meat and vegetables is a classic stew.

clue.text: Inferior race, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a race is run over a course, as in a racecourse

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain race of people is inferior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is a racecourse, not an ethnic group; COURSE spoken matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rough and low in quality is of poorer, lesser grade.

clue.text: Morale of mate spooked by ghost

indicators.note: spooked, frightened and jumpy, says the letters of mate are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a ghost is a spirit

explanation.surface: A friend's nerve is shaken by seeing a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spooked' rearranges MATE into TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective morale is the shared confidence and loyalty of a group working together.

clue.text: Shot a line after private action that backfired?

indicators.note: after places the shot, a and line behind the word for private

parts.note: something private is your own
a shot is a go, an attempt

explanation.surface: A soldier fired a round and spun a yarn following a failed manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot a line' reads as boasting and 'private' as a soldier's rank, but neither is used in that sense; 'after' sets the shot behind the private piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring into your own net is the classic sporting act that rebounds on the doer.

clue.text: Nothing charged for fruit

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
a charged wire is live, carrying current

explanation.surface: Fruit given away free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests price, but here it is electrical: a live wire.
explanation.definitionFit: The small oily stone fruit of the Mediterranean tree is a fruit.

clue.text: Poets felt that novel never got started

indicators.note: novel, meaning new and different, says these letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Poets felt that a certain novel never really got going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it is the anagram signal for POETS FELT THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that fails to leave the starting gate is stranded at the start, idiomatically beaten from the outset.

clue.text: A diamond ring, returned in the end

indicators.note: returned means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a diamond is a gem
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A diamond ring was given back when the relationship finally ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns A, GEM and O round as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet, so idiomatically the finish, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Football club stadium, around southern end of Clerkenwell

indicators.note: around says the arena wraps round the letter for southern

parts.note: a stadium is an arena

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of Clerkenwell

explanation.surface: A football club's ground lies near the southern edge of Clerkenwell, a district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside ARENA, then the last letter L of Clerkenwell is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The north London side is one of England's best-known professional football teams.

clue.text: Carnival provided retired with free teas

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the word for provided is read in reverse

parts.note: provided, as in on condition that, means if

indicators.note: free says the letters of teas are released from their order

explanation.surface: A carnival where the free teas are offered to those retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses IF to FI; 'free' rearranges TEAS into ESTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive celebration, a Spanish word for a festival or carnival.

clue.text: First and second entering woodland

indicators.note: entering puts the word for second inside the woodland word

parts.note: a forest is woodland
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Coming first and second as runners go into the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' wants to be a position in a race; it is the informal 'mo', a moment, and 'entering' puts it inside the woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading, most prominent or chief: synonym for first in rank.

clue.text: Repartee, as such, involving one with banner

indicators.note: involving means the outer phrase takes in the other pieces

parts.note: per se is Latin for as such, in itself
I is the Roman numeral one
a banner is a flag

explanation.surface: Witty exchanges, of the sort that involve a person waving a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: I and FLAG go inside PER SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Light, teasing banter between people is witty, playful exchange.

clue.text: Relative at sea?

parts.note: a family relation that sails: a vessel built to the same design as another, like a sibling of the fleet

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel of identical design to another is its nautical relation, playfully a female sibling afloat.

clue.text: Some keep on going, causing a stink

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people keep going on, raising a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a bad smell; the clue's phrase works as a noun-like description of foul odour.

clue.text: Its inhabitants may be crackers

parts.note: crackers reads as mad, but these residents are dry savoury biscuits kept in a jar on the sideboard

explanation.definitionFit: A container for biscuits holds crackers among its contents, a British household item.

clue.text: Jazz musicians, loud, restrained on radio

parts.note: loud, as in large and flashy, means big

indicators.note: on radio signals that the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: restrained, held back by prohibition, means banned

explanation.surface: Jazz players were loud, so they were kept off the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: BANNED spoken matches BAND; BIG comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jazz ensemble of the swing era is a group of jazz musicians.

clue.text: Gap made by a brisk Yorkshire river

parts.note: pert can mean lively or brisk
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A gap formed by a fast-flowing river in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure flows through Wensleydale in Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening or hole through which light passes is a gap.

clue.text: Make eyes at the Spanish turn making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback says the whole run returns, read backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a turn is a go, as in it's your go

explanation.surface: A Spanish performer's act makes a comeback and catches the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: EL and GO together, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare at someone with amorous interest is to eye them flirtatiously.

clue.text: Current party needs reforming

indicators.note: reforming, in the sense of forming again, says these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Today's political party is in need of reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' rearranges PARTY NEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemporary, belonging to now, is a synonym for current.

clue.text: President's first to speak in golf club

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of President's

parts.note: to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: The President is the first to speak at the golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: P from President's, then UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat-faced club used on the green is a type of golf club.

clue.text: When, for example, to make an analysis

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
say means for example

explanation.surface: Instructions about when, for instance, to carry out an analysis.
explanation.definitionFit: To test a metal or substance for its composition is to analyse it.

clue.text: Raised voice in argument after trip cut short

indicators.note: after puts the argument word behind the shortened trip word
cut short says the word for trip loses its last letter

parts.note: a trip is a fall
a set-to is an argument or fight

explanation.surface: Someone's voice rose in a row after a holiday was curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey but is a stumble: FALL cut short is FAL, then SET-TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A singing voice pitched above the natural range is a raised head voice.

clue.text: Push through American street

parts.note: thru is the American spelling of through

explanation.surface: Shoving one's way along an American street.
explanation.definitionFit: A forceful shove or forward drive is a push.

clue.text: Service at end of Lent produces a large collection

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of Lent

explanation.surface: A church service at the close of Lent produces a big collection plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' and 'collection' suggest church, but the service is military: RAF, then T.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a raft of things is a great many of them, a large number.

clue.text: Approach shot on golf course

definitions.meaning: the approach road leading up to a house is its driveway
the long opening stroke from the tee in golf

explanation.surface: An approach shot played on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a private road leading to a house and a long golf stroke from the tee.

clue.text: Careful in plant close to machinery

parts.note: thrift is a plant, the sea pink

indicators.note: close to picks the closing letter of machinery

explanation.surface: Being careful near plant and machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory, but it is the flower THRIFT; Y ends machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Economical and careful with money, frugal, is a synonym.
